question.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=4u+v-1,\,y=-u-3v+1.
$$

Let $P(-3,1)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4u+v-1 \\ -u-3v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4u+v \\ -u-3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$ 

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(-12,1).$
